synthesis: Across the family sketches, the reusable prime-polynomial and tail-bound architecture must be recentered according to the coherent prime-square layer: quadratic Dirichlet values acquire a positive half-log-log shift, whereas elliptic-curve twists acquire a negative half-log-log shift, matching the later conjectural positive and negative Gaussian centers; primitive characters retain the transferred architecture and are assigned zero conjectural center.
source_support: Unit u13 says the moment argument carries over to primitive characters with character orthogonality replacing the treatment of nondiagonal terms. Unit u14 explicitly contrasts quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the earlier setting, gives the prime-square contribution as about one half log log x, shifts the large-value threshold, and reuses the Section 4 route. Unit u15 again uses the analogous prime-power majorant, makes degrees at least three O(1), assigns the square layer the opposite half-log-log contribution, recenters the threshold, and reuses the tail argument. Unit u16 then states conjectural Gaussian means of zero, positive half-log-log, and negative half-log-log for the unitary, symplectic, and positive-sign orthogonal families, respectively.
nonparaphrase_operation: The synthesis aligns the local prime-power decompositions in u14 and u15 with the global center comparison in u16, showing that recentering is the modular adjustment that lets one proof architecture survive across families rather than merely grouping three family descriptions.
limits: These are GRH-conditional proof sketches, while the Gaussian laws are conjectural; the paper obtains one-sided upper-tail and moment bounds, not full distribution laws. Exact signs, constants, thresholds, and exponents are formula/OCR-sensitive. The bounded primitive-character unit does not itself isolate a negligible prime-square term, so only its transferred architecture and the zero center stated in u16 are retained. Full Selberg analogues additionally require most family members to have no zero very near 1/2, and the elliptic-curve comparison is restricted to positive functional-equation sign.
quality_reason: Accepted because u14 and u15 independently expose opposite square-layer recenterings and u16 jointly identifies the corresponding opposite family centers, while u13 establishes that the surrounding argument transfers through a changed orthogonality mechanism. The resulting mechanism depends on multiple sections and is unavailable from any one parent alone; the unsupported stronger wording about an explicitly demonstrated negligible unitary square term is excluded.
